## Research question

::: {.question}
How much does prognostics-based operation and maintenance change the cost of an offshore wind farm supplying electrolytic hydrogen?
:::

## My contribution

First author. Linked an operation-and-maintenance simulation developed with University of Strathclyde collaborators to the system techno-economic optimization.

## Method

Two-stage approach: Monte Carlo operation-and-maintenance simulation, then techno-economic optimization for a Gulf of Mexico site supplying Houston-area refineries.

## Key findings

::: {.findings}
- Prognostics-based maintenance lowered wind operation-and-maintenance cost by about 10% and downtime by about 11%.
- At the system level, the levelized cost of hydrogen fell by about 2%.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Boundary conditions"}
Single site; 2012 wind-resource data paired with 2022 electricity prices; maintenance parameters from the collaborators' framework.
:::
